title: What the rocks gave us
ncert_source_note: Plan listed 12th_p2_ch07 but that chapter does not exist in geo_universe.json. Correct file is 12th_p1_ch07_mineral_and_energy_resources — verified by node lookup.

concepts.label: Igneous Rock
concepts.what: Rocks formed by cooling and solidification of magma or lava; intrusive types (granite) cool slowly underground, coarse-grained; extrusive types (basalt) cool fast at surface, fine-grained.

concepts.label: Granite
concepts.what: Coarse-grained intrusive igneous rock composed of quartz, feldspar, and mica; hard, light-coloured; forms continental interiors and ancient shields.

concepts.label: Basalt
concepts.what: Fine-grained extrusive igneous rock; dark, dense; poured out at surface; Deccan Plateau is basalt at continental scale — 66 Ma lava outpour, now parent of fertile black soils.

concepts.label: Sedimentary Rock
concepts.what: Formed by weathering, transport, deposition, and lithification of sediments; layered; fossil-bearing; hosts coal, oil, and natural gas in sedimentary basins.

concepts.label: Sandstone
concepts.what: Mechanically formed sedimentary rock of cemented sand grains (mainly quartz); common building stone.

concepts.label: Limestone
concepts.what: Organically formed sedimentary rock of calcium carbonate (CaCO3); raw material for cement and steelmaking flux; wide domestic distribution lowers transport costs.

concepts.label: Metamorphic Rock
concepts.what: Existing rocks transformed by heat and pressure without fully melting; marble from limestone, slate from shale, schist and gneiss from igneous rocks under mountain-building pressure.

concepts.label: Marble
concepts.what: Non-foliated metamorphic rock formed from limestone under heat and pressure; used in construction and sculpture.

concepts.label: Slate
concepts.what: Fine-grained foliated metamorphic rock from low-grade metamorphism of shale; splits into thin layers; used as roofing material.

concepts.label: Rock Cycle
concepts.what: Continuous process linking all three rock families — igneous weathers to sediment, which lithifies and may metamorphose, and eventually melts back to magma.

concepts.label: Mineral
concepts.what: Naturally occurring inorganic substance with a definite chemical composition and characteristic physical properties; over 3,000 known; only a handful form common rocks.

concepts.label: Ore Formation Processes
concepts.what: Geological processes concentrating minerals into economically viable deposits — hydrothermal deposition in fractures, sedimentary accumulation, weathering-residual concentration, placer deposits on coastlines.

concepts.label: Mineral Classification
concepts.what: Three working categories — metallic (ferrous: iron, manganese, chromite; non-ferrous: copper, gold, bauxite); non-metallic (limestone, mica, gypsum, salt); energy minerals (coal, petroleum, uranium, thorium).

concepts.label: World Mineral Distribution
concepts.what: Global mineral map is a map of ancient geological events — Congo cobalt, South Africa gold/platinum/chromite/diamonds, Russia gas/nickel, Middle East petroleum, Australia iron/bauxite, Chile copper/lithium, China rare earths.

concepts.label: Tethys Sea and Middle East Petroleum
concepts.what: Ancient Tethys Sea separated Gondwana from Laurasia; shallow marine basins deposited organic material that became Middle East petroleum reserves after pressure-cooking under sediment.

concepts.label: India's Four Mineral Belts
concepts.what: NE Plateau (Chotanagpur — Gondwana shield), SW Plateau (Karnataka/Goa — Dharwar system), NW Belt (Aravalli — ancient non-ferrous), Himalayan Belt (under-explored); each belt reflects distinct geological history.

concepts.label: North-Eastern Plateau Belt (Chotanagpur)
concepts.what: Precambrian shield across Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, West Bengal; densest mineral zone in India — coal, iron ore, manganese, mica, bauxite, chromite, copper concentrated by 2 billion years of geological time.

concepts.label: Singhbhum (Iron Ore and Copper)
concepts.what: Jharkhand district; primary location for iron ore and copper within the NE Plateau Belt; sits on Precambrian Dharwar-type basement rocks.

concepts.label: Hazaribagh-Kodarma Mica Belt
concepts.what: Districts in Jharkhand; produce India's highest-quality muscovite mica used in electrical and electronics insulation; India was world's leading mica exporter through the 20th century.

concepts.label: South-Western Plateau Belt (Karnataka/Goa)
concepts.what: Iron ore at Kudremukh and Bellary-Hospet (Karnataka), gold at Kolar (closed 2001) and Hutti; Goa iron ore exported through Mormugao port to Japan and South Korea.

concepts.label: Kolar Gold Mine
concepts.what: One of world's deepest gold mines, Karnataka; produced ore for over a century; closed 2001 after exhaustion; historically India's largest gold source.

concepts.label: North-Western Belt (Aravalli)
concepts.what: Aravalli Range through Rajasthan into Gujarat; among Earth's oldest fold mountains; non-ferrous metals from ancient hydrothermal processes — copper at Khetri, lead-zinc at Zawar and Rampura-Agucha.

concepts.label: Khetri Copper Mine
concepts.what: Rajasthan; one of India's largest copper-mining complexes, in the Aravalli belt.

concepts.label: Zawar and Rampura-Agucha Lead-Zinc Mines
concepts.what: Rajasthan; Zawar is one of world's oldest continuously worked mines (ancient smelting evidence); Rampura-Agucha among world's largest zinc-lead deposits.

concepts.label: Himalayan Mineral Belt
concepts.what: Under-explored — copper, lead, zinc, cobalt, tungsten identified in scattered pockets; young Himalayan erosion has not yet exposed deeper deposits; strategic future unwritten.

concepts.label: India's Iron Ore
concepts.what: India holds some of world's largest haematite reserves; among top global producers — Singhbhum (Jharkhand), Bailadila (Chhattisgarh), Kudremukh (Karnataka), Keonjhar-Sundergarh (Odisha leads production).

concepts.label: Bailadila Iron Ore Complex
concepts.what: Fourteen-deposit complex in Bastar hills, Chhattisgarh; much exported to Japan and South Korea under trade arrangements dating to the 1960s.

concepts.label: Haematite and Magnetite Grades
concepts.what: Haematite — high iron content, found across Gondwana-shield zones (Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh); magnetite — harder to process, found in Karnataka.

concepts.label: India's Coal
concepts.what: India among world's three largest coal producers; 98% is Gondwana coal (Permian, ~250 Ma); predominantly non-coking bituminous; fuels ~55% of electricity generation.

concepts.label: Damodar Valley Coalfields
concepts.what: India's largest coalfield cluster — Raniganj (West Bengal), Jharia (Jharkhand, largest by reserve, underground fires burning over a century), Bokaro, Giridih.

concepts.label: Gondwana Coal
concepts.what: Permian-age coal (~250 Ma) from buried Gondwana forests; 98% of India's reserves; in Damodar Valley and Mahanadi, Godavari, Wardha basins.

concepts.label: Tertiary Coal (Northeast India)
concepts.what: Younger coal (15-20 Ma) in Assam, Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh; lower carbon content than Gondwana coal.

concepts.label: India's Coking Coal Deficit
concepts.what: India imports millions of tonnes of coking coal annually; domestic coal is overwhelmingly non-coking bituminous; steelmaking requires coking coal that India's geology does not supply adequately.

concepts.label: Mica in India
concepts.what: India was world's leading mica exporter; Hazaribagh-Kodarma (Jharkhand) produces highest-quality muscovite; also Nellore (Andhra Pradesh) and Jaipur-Bhilwara-Udaipur (Rajasthan).

concepts.label: Bauxite in India
concepts.what: Ore of aluminium found in laterite rocks; Odisha leads (Kalahandi, Sambalpur); also Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Gujarat.

concepts.label: Manganese in India
concepts.what: Used in steel alloying and battery technology; mainly from Odisha, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh.

concepts.label: Limestone Distribution in India
concepts.what: Widely distributed — Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan; proximity to cement plants and steel mills economically significant given limestone's low value-to-weight ratio.

concepts.label: Gypsum in India
concepts.what: Used in cement and fertiliser; mainly from Rajasthan.

concepts.label: Salt Production in India
concepts.what: Two sources — sea brine evaporation (Gujarat's Kutch coast is largest; Tamil Nadu coast) and lake brine from Sambhar lake (Rajasthan, largest inland salt lake in India).

concepts.label: Sambhar Lake
concepts.what: Largest inland salt lake in India, Rajasthan; produces salt from lake brine evaporation; located in the North-Western Belt zone.

concepts.label: Kerala-Tamil Nadu Coastal Heavy Mineral Suite
concepts.what: Beach sands of Kerala-TN coast contain ilmenite and rutile (titanium sources), zircon, sillimanite, and monazite; concentrated by marine processes; legally a strategic resource.

concepts.label: Monazite
concepts.what: Mineral in Kerala-TN beach sands containing thorium and rare-earth elements; prescribed substance — only government bodies can process or export it.

concepts.label: India's Thorium-Based Nuclear Strategy
concepts.what: India's three-stage nuclear programme designed to eventually use thorium as fuel; monazite sands hold one of world's largest known thorium reserves; current reactor technology cannot yet use it.

concepts.label: India's Petroleum
concepts.what: India imports ~85% of crude oil; geology is coal-rich and oil-poor; major fields — Digboi (Assam, 1889), Mumbai High (largest), KG basin, Cambay (Gujarat), Barmer (Rajasthan).

concepts.label: Digboi Oilfield
concepts.what: Assam; discovered 1889; one of world's oldest continuously worked oilfields; India's first oil discovery.

concepts.label: Mumbai High Offshore Field
concepts.what: India's largest producing oilfield in Arabian Sea; discovered 1974; accounted for ~40% of domestic crude at peak; reserves declining.

concepts.label: Krishna-Godavari Basin
concepts.what: Major natural gas province offshore Andhra Pradesh (Reliance D6 block); emerged 2000s as significant gas source; part of India's eastern coastal energy zone.

concepts.label: Natural Gas in India
concepts.what: Same geography as petroleum — Mumbai High, KG basin, Cambay, Tripura, Rajasthan; GAIL built national pipeline network to move gas from producing areas to industrial consumers.

concepts.label: Solar Energy in India
concepts.what: ~300 clear sunny days annually especially in Rajasthan and Gujarat; major parks — Bhadla (Rajasthan, Thar Desert), Pavagada (Karnataka), Kurnool (Andhra Pradesh).

concepts.label: International Solar Alliance
concepts.what: India co-founded; headquartered at Gurugram; groups tropical countries to accelerate solar deployment; energy diplomacy rooted in India's high-insolation geography.

concepts.label: Wind Energy in India
concepts.what: Strongest along southern peninsula coasts and Western Ghats passes; major farms — Muppandal (Tamil Nadu, largest in Asia), Jaisalmer, Kutch coast; 5th-largest installed wind capacity globally.

concepts.label: Nuclear Energy in India
concepts.what: Uranium at Jaduguda (Jharkhand, main mine) and Tummalapalle (Andhra Pradesh); limited uranium reserves; three-stage programme makes thorium the long-term fuel base.

concepts.label: Jaduguda Uranium Mine
concepts.what: Main operational uranium mine in India, Singhbhum district, Jharkhand; only major uranium mining complex currently in operation.

concepts.label: Geothermal Energy in India
concepts.what: Sites at Manikaran (Himachal Pradesh) and Puga Valley (Ladakh); not commercially significant yet.

concepts.label: Tidal Energy in India
concepts.what: Theoretically feasible in Gulf of Kutch and Gulf of Khambhat (large tidal ranges); no commercial plant exists.

concepts.label: Adivasi-Mineral Structural Overlap
concepts.what: India's Gondwana coal and Chotanagpur minerals are concentrated in Scheduled V tribal homelands — thin soils on ancient shield rock left land as forest; mining directly conflicts with Adivasi customary forest and land rights.

concepts.label: PESA Act 1996
concepts.what: Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act; extends gram sabha governance to Schedule V tribal areas; requires gram sabha consent for land acquisition in tribal regions.

concepts.label: Forest Rights Act 2006
concepts.what: Recognises forest rights of Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers on land they have historically occupied; intended to remedy colonial-era dispossession of forest access.
